To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
coronary computed tomographic angiography (CCTA) has the ability to detect coronary artery disease (CAD) in patients with low to intermediate pre-test probability of CAD.

the prognostic utility and diagnostic accuracy of CTA for the prediction of future cardiovascular events in patients without modifiable risk factors is similar to that in the overall CONFIRM registry population.

The prevalence of coronary artery disease was 2.5% in patients with no coronary artery disease risk factor, 5.6% in patients with only traditional risk factors and 10.7% in patients with traditional and metabolic risk factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a novel approach to the problem of the problem of the Long term prognostics utility of coronary CT angiography in patients with modifiable coronary artery disease risk factors: Results of the 5 year follow-up of the CONFIR International Multicenter Registry.
the long-term prognostic utility (LTPU) of CTA in patients with no MCDRFs.
the development of a novel method for the analysis of the data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

coronary artery calcium (CAC) is a strong and reliable predictor of future cardiac events, especially in high-risk patients, and that CAC is a better predictor of events than the Framingham risk score.
the use of coronary CT angiogram is a very useful and accurate method of detecting coronary artery disease and is superior to stress testing in the diagnosis of obstructive CAD.
the use of CT coronary angiography in patients who have no modifiable risk factors and are at a low risk for cardiovascular disease is not recommended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the long-term prognostic utility for patients with no modifi able coronary artery disease (CAD) risk factors is not as robust as patients with traditional risk factors.
the long-term prognostic utility for CTA is similar in patients with and without modifiable CVD risk factors.
the long-term prognostic utility is limited for patients with no modifi able coronary artery disease (CAD) risk factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we can now identify a group of patients with no modifi able risk factors for coronary artery disease (CAD) who have a high risk of adverse cardiovascular (CV) events, and we can identify them with a noninvasive test, namely coronary computed tomography (CT) angiography (CCTA).
the use of CT angiography in the absence of modifiable risk factors is associated with a very good prognosis.
we can now use a single coronary CTA to identify patients who are at high risk for adverse events, including death and heart attacks, in the future.
